questions.prompt: Why did Maya first join the gardening club?
questions.sentence: Maya joined her school's gardening club in April, mostly because her best friend was a member. At first, she found the work boring: pulling weeds, carrying water, and waiting for seeds to grow. In June, however, the club decided to grow vegetables for a local food bank. Maya was put in charge of the tomatoes. Every morning before class, she checked the plants and wrote notes in a small notebook. When the first tomatoes turned red in July, she was surprised by how proud she felt. By the end of summer, the club had given more than 60 kilograms of vegetables to the food bank. Maya now says that gardening taught her patience, and that helping others made the waiting worthwhile.
choices: Because her best friend was a member.
Because she wanted to help a food bank.
Because her teacher told her to.

questions.prompt: What is a "car-free day"?
questions.sentence: Many cities around the world are trying to reduce traffic in their centers. One popular idea is the "car-free day," when cars are not allowed on certain streets. On these days, people walk, ride bicycles, or use public transportation. Supporters say that car-free days make the air cleaner and give people a chance to enjoy the city in a new way. Street musicians play, and cafes put tables outside. However, some shop owners worry that fewer customers will come if they cannot drive. Studies from several cities show mixed results: some shops lose sales, while others, especially restaurants, actually earn more. Most experts agree that car-free days work best when the city also improves its buses and trains.
choices: A day when cars are not allowed on certain streets.
A day when all shops are closed.
A day when bus rides are free.
A day when people must buy new cars.
questions.explanation: 第2文で定義されている。

questions.prompt: Which is NOT mentioned as something octopuses can do?
questions.sentence: Octopuses are among the most intelligent animals in the ocean. They can open jars, escape from tanks, and even recognize individual people. Unlike humans, an octopus has most of its nerve cells in its arms, not in its brain. This means each arm can taste, touch, and react to things on its own. Octopuses are also masters of disguise. Special cells in their skin allow them to change color and texture in less than a second, helping them hide from enemies or surprise their prey. Sadly, most octopuses live only one or two years. Scientists are still trying to understand how such a short-lived animal became so clever.

questions.prompt: Why did Tom Walker write this letter?
questions.sentence:
Dear Ms. Suzuki,
Thank you for visiting our museum last week with your students. We hope they enjoyed the dinosaur exhibition. We are writing to tell you about a new program starting in October. Every Saturday, museum staff will hold a free workshop for high school students called "Be a Fossil Hunter." Participants will learn how scientists clean and study fossils, and they will be able to take home a copy of a real fossil. Because space is limited to 15 students per workshop, please register online at least one week in advance. We would be grateful if you could share this information with your students.
Sincerely,
Tom Walker, Education Department

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what does the brain do during sleep?
questions.sentence: Sleep is not just a time when the body rests. Researchers have found that during sleep, the brain organizes the information it received during the day. Memories that seem important are strengthened, while less useful ones fade. This is one reason why students who sleep well often remember what they studied better than those who stay up all night. Teenagers need about eight to ten hours of sleep, but many get much less. Using smartphones in bed is one common cause, because the bright screen can make it harder to fall asleep. Experts suggest putting devices away at least an hour before going to bed.
choices: It makes the body grow taller.
It organizes the information from the day.
questions.explanation: the brain organizes the information it received during the day。

questions.prompt: Why did Kenji start walking dogs?
questions.sentence: Kenji wanted to buy a new bicycle, but it cost 40,000 yen. Instead of asking his parents for money, he decided to earn it himself. He started walking dogs for elderly neighbors on weekends and charged 500 yen per walk. At first he had only two customers, but word spread quickly, and soon he was walking eight dogs every weekend. After four months, he had saved enough money. When he finally bought the bicycle, he realized he did not want to stop walking dogs. The neighbors had become his friends, and they often invited him in for tea. Kenji decided to keep working, and he now saves part of his earnings for college.
choices: To earn money for a new bicycle.
Because his parents told him to.
